terms.gloss: up and down, to and fro
terms.grammar: two adverbs, “upwards, downwards”; also sūrsum ac deorsum
evidence: Ter. Eun. 2.2.47: nē sūrsum deorsum cursitēs (Lewis & Short s.v. deorsum)
Cic. N.D. 2.84: nātūrīs sūrsum deorsum, ultrō citrō commeantibus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of movement this way and that. With a verb of turning it is also “topsy-turvy”: omnia ista sūrsum deorsum fortūna versāvit (Sen. Ep. 44.4, Lewis & Short s.v. sūrsum; see topsy-turvy).

phrases.latin: cum terra quatitur et sūrsum ac deorsum movētur
phrases.english: when the earth shakes and moves up and down

sources: Lewis & Short: sursum · Lewis & Short: deorsum
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 110.
